description: Pull-up holding the DAC8568 CLR inactive, with a bring-up pad
notes: THE WATCHDOG IS DELETED (U-WATCHDOG, R-WDT, C-WDT all gone), so CLR has no driver and is tied INACTIVE - pulled high. A solder pad to ground beside it lets CLR be asserted BY HAND, which E7-E10 want anyway: a 99ms watchdog would have fought every 'write a code, read the meter' step of pitch calibration. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual CLR still parks at zero scale. Do NOT write ClearIgnore

description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THIS WAS PULLED TO AVDD AND THAT GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38 verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' Same page: the internal LDAC register defaults to 0x00, and 'if the LDAC register bit is set to 0, the DAC channel is controlled by the LDAC pin'. So register at default + pin high = the buffer-to-DAC-register transfer is BLOCKED, and with no MISO firmware can never discover it - a module that accepts every word and moves no output. Same class as the pull-DOWN-on-CLR defect the previous redraw caught, opposite polarity, same page. | The consequence the old row claimed still holds: a hardware LDAC was considered and declined, so the six populated channels update as each word lands. BUT SBAS430E Table 11 p.36 offers 'Write to DAC input register Ch X and update all DAC registers (SW LDAC)' - five plain writes then one update-all as the last word of each pass gives a SIMULTANEOUS update in the six words already budgeted, taking the 100-200us CLR-exit window to zero for no parts and no ninth conductor
